correctness.rationale: The four row-coverage classes exhaust the eight subsets of each three-vertex column with correct weights. A vertex is dominated precisely when each cyclic triple covers all three rows. The 16-state directed pair graph therefore counts the complete polynomial by tr(T^n) for all n>=3. The finite determinant identity det(XI-T)=X^7 A(X)B(X) is symbolically recomputed from all matrix entries by verify.py. At z=-1 its roots have multiplicities 1 three times, -1 twice, +i twice, and -i twice, yielding 9 at n divisible by four and 1 otherwise. Independent direct adjacency enumeration checks the full polynomial for n=3 through 6. Finite checks are not substitutes for the exact transfer proof; cycles of sizes 1 and 2 are excluded.

originality.rationale: The six actual semantic research-database queries and targeted literature searches found no matching closed all-circumference polynomial or signed four-period law for P_3 strong-product C_n. The most relevant original full texts establish free-boundary king-board signed behavior (Moore and Mertens, 2024) and algorithms for Cartesian cylinders and noncyclic king boards (Mertens, 2024). Neither logically implies the present cubic-sextic factorization. An older graph-family paper treats independent domination rather than the ordinary domination polynomial; its full text was inaccessible, explicitly recorded as a residual risk. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not certification of publication priority.

value.rationale: The 2024 king-board parity result identifies cyclic boundaries as producing nontrivial exceptional behavior. Determining the entire ordinary domination polynomial for every three-row king cylinder at once, by a fixed-degree nine-root algebraic expression, is a natural exact enumeration of a canonical graph strip. The derived 1-versus-9 parity law at mod-four circumferences exhibits a nontrivial structural boundary effect. The explicit row-state factorization can motivate other fixed-width families. It is not an arbitrary finite table or routine renaming of the source Cartesian-cylinder algorithms.
